items.title: v5.22.0: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
items.abstract_or_text: ## New Models ### Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe. Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union. #### Key Features Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices: - **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert. - **1M context length**, for long-context workloads. - **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. - **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request. Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities: - **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run. - **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights. - **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union. - **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts. - **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement. - **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests. - **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window. The model is released under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. #### Recommended Settings - **Reasoning Effort**: - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`. - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage. - **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: - `temperature=1.0` - `top_p=0.95` - **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. - **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. - **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille ## Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and `is_trainable` is now `True`. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. Separately, the AMD CI image now install * FP8 backward: chunked expert dequant, skip autograd.Function at inference (#50117) by @ArthurZucker in [#50117] * Train adapters on top of FP8 weights items.abstract_or_text: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aa86ec7-6444-4bed-bfdc-0445e99bea0d ## Features ### 🔥 Mistral Large 4: fine-tune a 1T-parameter model on one node TRL now supports [`mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B): 1T parameters, 52B active. The new [LoRA example](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/tree/main/examples/sft_mistral_large_4) fine-tunes it with `SFTTrainer` **on a single 8×B300 node, on top of its FP8 weights**: the experts are split 8 ways with token dispatch, everything else is sharded across the 8 GPUs at load time by transformers' `DistributedConfig`, and LoRA trains attention and the dense and shared-expert MLPs. Measured: **32.7k tokens per step in ~8 s, 142 GiB per GPU**, with packing and assistant-only loss on reasoning conversations. ```python training_args = SFTConfig( model_init_kwargs={ "dtype": "auto", # keep the FP8 weights "distributed_config": DistributedConfig(fsdp_size=8, ep_size=8), }, packing=True, assistant_only_loss=True, ... ) trainer = SFTTrainer(model="mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B", args=training_args, peft_config=LoraConfig(...), ...) ``` `assistant_only_loss=True` works out of the box: TRL ships a training chat template that matches the released checkpoint's, including its `reasoning_effort` levels (`low`, `medium`, `high`). Needs `transformers>=5.22.0`, `peft>=0.21.0` and `accelerate>=1.15.0`. * Add Mistral Large 4 by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8017 * Sync the Mistral Large 4 chat template with the released checkpoint by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8018 ### 🎯 Unbiased importance sampling under top-k, top-p and min-p vLLM normalizes its log-probabilities over the tokens left after `top_k`, `top_p` and `min_p` filtering, while the trainer normalized over the whole vocabulary. Every sampled token's log-ratio was off by the log of the probability mass the filter kept, so the vLLM importance sampling ratio was biased towards 0 (around 1e-4 instead of 1 with `top_p=0.9`). The trainers now normalize over the candidate set each token was sampled from, following Keep Sampling Mask from [DeepSeek-V3.2](https://huggingface.co/papers/2512.02556). * AsyncGRPO: renormalize log-probs over the top-k/top-p candidate set by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7627 * GRPO: renormalize log-probs over the top-k/top-p candidate set (vLLM colocate mode, vLLM >= 0.28; server mode will follow) by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7866 * Require `top_k` with `min_p` in AsyncGRPO so the importance sampling ratio stays unbiased by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7937 * Track the support maximum in the chunked log-prob kernel, so a far-below-max candidate set no longer gives a log-probability of 0 and non-finite gradients, by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7983 **💥 What this changes for you.** vLLM bounds the candidate set it returns with `top_k`, so with vLLM and the importance sampling correction on (the default), `GRPOConfig` now raises when `top_p 0.0` is set without `top_k > 0`. Set `top_k` (e.g. `top_k=512`), or `vllm_importance_sampling_correction=False`. ### ⚖️ Score centering is the default AsyncGRPO objective AsyncGRPO's old log-probs are the vLLM sampler's, so its ratio mixes staleness with the numerical mismatch between the server and the trainer. With an FP8 sampler and a bf16 trainer, the clipped objective collapses: reward goes from 0.60 to 0.34 (FP8 weights) or 0.10 (FP8 weights + KV cache) by step 300, against 0.71 with a bf16 sampler. [Score centering](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.20807) with masked importance sampling is now the default (`score_centering=True`, `importance_sampling_min=0.5`, `importance_sampling_max=5.0`). With it, the FP8 sampler trains exactly like the bf16 one (0.72). It costs 15–20% of generation throughput. **💥 What this changes for you.** AsyncGRPO runs now train with a different objective by default, and tokens whose ratio to the sampler falls outside `[0.5, 5.0]` are dropped. Set `score_centering=False` to keep the clipped objective. by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7760 ### 🚀 Faster AsyncGRPO rollouts and packing * **Adaptive in-flight cap from the vLLM load**: the rollout worker follows the server's KV cache usage instead of admitting a fixed `max_inflight_tasks`, so requests stop queueing and being preempted on the server. No new config: everything is read from the server. By @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7610 * **Filter zero-advantage groups** (DAPO's dynamic sampling): groups whose rollouts all got the same reward, or none of which could be scored, no longer cost a forward and backward. By @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7609 * **Pack the sampling mask ragged and pad it on the device**: `TreeRow.pack` goes from 250 s to 31 s on rank 0 over a 15-step run, and from 1040 ms to 66 ms on a 28k-token multi-turn row. By @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7798 * Keep filling a micro-batch when another row has free room by @clementtisseau in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7793 * Use FlashAttention-4 on Blackwell GPUs in async GRPO and async distillation by @lewtun in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7792 ### 🌳 Tree attention for linear-attention hybrids Tree packing (v1.16) now supports the Gated DeltaNet hybrids: Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Qwen3-Next and OLMo-Hybrid. Since v1.16 the trainer refused them at init; before it, sequence packing accepted them but was silently wrong on them. The causal convolution and the delta-rule recurrence now follow the tree instead of the row, through FLA's chunked kernels. by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7686 ### 🎚️ Precise chunked log-probabilities The chunked log-probability and KL/JSD heads get the two precision fixes from [A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy](https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.31642): confident targets keep their small gradients, and matching teachers produce zero gradients. [Entropy-preserving reinforcement learning](https://huggingface.co/papers/2603.11682) (Appendix B.4) reports the same high-confidence policy-gradient issue. * Fix chunked loss precision by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7882 * Fix the fused log-prob/entropy backward on strided inputs (shifted views from SFT/DPO) by @winglian in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7890 ### 🔀 X-Token cross-tokenizer distillation in GOLD `GOLDTrainer` gets off-policy cross-tokenizer distillation based on [X-Token](https://huggingface.co/papers/2605.21699): set `lmbda=0.0` and `xtoken_loss_type="p_kl"` or `"h_kl"` with a precomputed projection matrix. * Add X-Token cross-tokenizer KD to GOLD trainer by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/6126 * Support byte-fallback tokenizers (Gemma) in GOLD byte-offset alignment by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8010 ### 🟥 Training on AMD GPUs TRL's trainers now run on AMD Instinct GPUs through PyTorch's ROCm build, with a [guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/amd_gpus) and an AMD CI job that runs the test suite on every PR. * Document training on AMD GPUs by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7844 * Add AMD/ROCm CI by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/5918 ### 🧩 More models * **Beam**: tiny model, SFT/DPO/GRPO/RLOO tests, GRPO tool calling, and a LoRA SFT example on one 8×B300 node. Needs `transformers>=5.20.1`. By @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7629 * **Mistral Medium 3.5**: training chat template for assistant-only loss by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7940 * **LFM2.5-24B-A2B** (and LFM2.5-2.6B's current template) for tool calling by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7753 * **LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct and LFM2.5-VL-450M** for tool calling by @albertvillanova in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7909, https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7910 and https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7911 * **TRL's own Qwen3 training template** for response parsing, so a tokenizer saved by assistant-only SFT works in GRPO, by @edbeeching in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8007 ### Other * Accept instantiated models in `AsyncGRPOTrainer` by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/6676, and port instantiated models, MoE aux loss and the injected-worker LoRA name to `AsyncDistillationTrainer` by @kashif in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7984 * Save AsyncGRPO and AsyncDistillation checkpoints in the mixed-precision dtype instead of fp32 by @AmineDiro in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7807 * **Require `top_k` with `top_p 0.0` in GRPO with vLLM importance sampling** (see above) by @albertvillanova in items.abstract_or_text: sycl : vectorize reordered-layout dequantization stores (Q4_0, K-quants, IQ3, MXFP4) (#30976) * sycl : widen reordered q4_0 dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_0 conversion kernel processed one qs byte per work-item with two scalar stores, strided 16 elements apart. Give it the same treatment the Q8_0 kernel got in #30775: a flat sycl::range launch with four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. Same float math and rounding as the scalar kernel; output is bit-identical. The existing k % QK4_0 == 0 assert guarantees whole 32-element blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The now-unreferenced scalar reorder kernel is removed. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +6.4% to +7.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_0 models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill and decode unchanged; PPL within run noise. * sycl : vectorize reordered q4_K dequantization stores The reordered-layout Q4_K conversion kernel already loads its quantized inputs through sycl::vec but writes the dequantized results with scalar stores. Build the results in a vec register and emit two vector stores instead. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill (prefill after decode on a reorder-installed tensor): +14.7% to +15.3% pp512/pp2048 on Q4_K-dominant models (tested up to 27B dense); fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q5_K dequantization to vec4 loads/stores The reordered-layout Q5_K conversion kernel gave each thread only four outputs fed by scalar ql/qh byte loads plus a local-memory scale broadcast, so the stores were never its bottleneck: widening the stores alone measured within noise on mixed-quant models and +0.5% on a q5_K-dominant model. Re-decompose to 32 threads per block, each consuming four consecutive ql and qh bytes and emitting two aligned vec stores; a 4-element run shares one scale pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill on a q5_K-dominant 27B model: +3.6% pp512/pp2048 over the scalar kernel; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. The GET_ROWS reorder path moves to the same 32-thread decomposition. * sycl : remap reordered q6_K dequantization to vec4 stores The reordered-layout Q6_K conversion kernel wrote four scalars per thread, strided 32 elements apart, each pair of neighbors sharing neither instruction stream nor store transaction. Re-decompose the same 64-thread work-group so each thread emits one aligned vec : a 4-element run shares one 16-element scale group, one ql nibble source and one qh bit pair, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +28.7% pp512/pp2048 on a Q6_K 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered q3_K dequantization stores Each thread of the reordered-layout Q3_K conversion kernel already computes four consecutive outputs; build them in a vec register and emit one vector store instead of four scalars. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +16.8% pp512/pp2048 on a Q3_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : vectorize reordered iq3_xxs/iq3_s dequantization stores Both reordered-layout IQ3 conversion kernels write eight contiguous outputs per thread as scalar stores (four from each grid lookup). Build two vec registers and emit two vector stores. Same per-element math; output is bit-identical. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +20.3% to +21.1% pp512/pp2048 on IQ3_XXS- and IQ3_S-dominant 27B models; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : remap reordered q2_K dequantization to vec4 stores Re-decompose the reordered-layout Q2_K conversion kernel the same way as Q6_K: one aligned vec per thread instead of four scalars strided 32 apart. A 4-element run shares one scale byte and one 2-bit lane, so the per-element math and the output are identical to the scalar kernel. Arc Pro B70, primed prefill: +13.1% pp512/pp2048 on a Q2_K-dominant 27B model; fresh-layout prefill, decode and PPL unchanged. * sycl : widen reordered mxfp4 dequantization stores Give the reordered-layout MXFP4 conversion kernel the same flat sycl::range launch as Q4_0: four qs bytes (8 outputs) per work-item inside one 32-element block and two vec stores. Same LUT lookups and per-block scale; output is bit-identical. The k % QK_MXFP4 == 0 assert guarantees whole blocks, so the k/8 launch covers every row exactly. The old scalar kernel is removed. The reordered layout for MXFP4 is installed on the MoE expert path (reorder_qw_mxfp4_moe); dense MXFP4 tensors keep the normal layout. Arc Pro B70, MXFP4 MoE 20B model: +57% pp2048 / +61% pp512 prefill (primed and fresh alike), decode unchanged, PPL within the model's run-to-run noise. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - The model output then had the source's size, and copying it back overran the result buffer, which crashes test-backend-ops on the SCALE view cases. Slice the input with process_view_input_new, as the other translators do. items.abstract_or_text: common, mtmd: bound control vector layer indices and M-RoPE position loops (#31336) * common: bound control vector layer indices by the model layer count A direction tensor layer index is parsed from the tensor name with no upper bound, and the buffer size and write offset are computed in int. A large index overflows both, so the accumulation writes before the start of the buffer. Pass the model layer count to the loader, reject indices above it like the existing zero index check, and compute the sizes in size_t. * mtmd: fill M-RoPE positions by whole merge tiles The position loops of the Qwen-VL, GLM, PaddleOCR and Qwen2.5-VL encoders hardcode a 2x2 merge inside a stride of n_merge, so a patch grid that is not a multiple of the merge writes past the positions buffer. Iterate over whole merge tiles with n_merge inner steps, which bounds the writes by the patch count and gives the same positions on aligned grids. PaddleOCR also requires a merge aligned image at graph build, as the Qwen-VL family already does. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11972/llama-b11972-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - A level is honored when it renders without raising and differently from the unknown level, which shows the template fallback. Levels sharing a render are aliases and the highest one is kept. items.abstract_or_text: llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape (#31243) * llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape qwen4exp (QSA) and glm5-next pick cache cells by index and no longer read the kq_mask values, but they still shaped the selection like the dense kq_mask. Build the selection as [n_kv, n_tokens] over the cache cells instead, and split it into the streams of the K view right before the attention.
